result: Hair follicles (HFs) expand perinatally in temporal concordance with Shh-responding dentate stem cells. Gli1-GFP+ hedgehog-responding cells were observed in forming HFs at E15.5, calvarial bones at later ages, and in the dentate gyrus from E17.5 onward. Despite dentate Gli1-GFP+ cell expansion, Shh expression was not detected in the dorsal cortex but was restricted to the ventral forebrain and HFs, which were the geographically closest Shh-expressing cells to the DG perinatally.
evaluation: Claims C4, C36-C41 provide converging anatomical and temporal evidence from Gli1-GFP reporter mice and in situ hybridization showing that HF expansion coincides with dentate stem cell proliferation and that HFs are the nearest Shh source to the developing dentate. The data from Figure 1 directly support these observations with appropriate controls and anatomical markers.

result: Specific inhibition of Shh from HFs using Krt14-Cre;Shhflx/flx mutants hindered development of Shh-responding dentate stem cells. These mutants showed loss of Ptch1 and Shh expression in the skin while ventral forebrain Shh was unaffected. Ki67+ dentate progenitors were significantly decreased at E17.5 and P1, and Prox1 staining showed more restricted neuronal localization in the mutant DG.
evaluation: Claims C5, C42-C44, C46 demonstrate a causal relationship between HF-derived Shh and dentate progenitor development using conditional genetics. The Krt14-Cre driver provides tissue-specific deletion, appropriate controls confirm specificity to skin versus brain Shh sources, and quantification shows statistically significant reductions in dentate progenitors (Figure 2).

result: Specific inhibition of Shh from epithelial sources using Msx2-Cre;Shhflx/flx mutants, which survived to adulthood, hindered development of Shh-responding dentate stem cells. These mutants showed decreased Ki67+ dentate progenitors at E16.5 and P3, with BrdU labeling confirming proliferation reduced to one-third of normal at P3. Cortical progenitors showed no significant difference, indicating selective effects on dentate progenitors.
evaluation: Claims C6, C47-C53 provide strong evidence using an alternative Cre driver (Msx2-Cre) that allows survival to adulthood. The selective effect on dentate versus cortical progenitors (C52, C53) strengthens the specificity argument. Quantification with both Ki67 and BrdU provides robust proliferation data (Figure 3), though the mechanism for long-term effects remains unclear.

result: Msx2-Cre;Shhflx/flx mutants showed diminished hedgehog-responding cells in the dentate. At P3, Ptch1-LacZ+ cells were reduced to one-third in mutants, Sox2+ dentate progenitor cells decreased at P1, and both radial glial stem cells and transit amplifying cells were reduced at P10 and P40. At P50, DCX-positive immature dentate neurons were significantly reduced (p < 0.005).
evaluation: Claims C54-C57 demonstrate long-lasting effects of perinatal epithelial Shh loss on dentate stem cell populations using multiple markers (Ptch1-LacZ, Sox2, Lef1, Blbp, Ki67, DCX). The persistence of deficits into adulthood (P40-P50) despite local Shh expression appearing by P3 suggests a critical developmental window, though mechanistic understanding is limited (Figure 4).

result: Hedgehog-responding cells in dermal mesenchyme were characterized and their role in dentate development was tested. Ptch1-LacZ expression was detected in calvarial sutures and developing bones at P3. Gli1+ cells at E17.5 were Pdgfrβ+, Vimentin+, and Desmin+ perivascular cells. Pdgfrb-Cre;Smoflx/flx mutants showed dramatically reduced skull size at P3 but only a slight decrease in Ki67+ dentate progenitors at E17.5 and P1, much less than in Shh mutants.
evaluation: Claims C86-C91 address potential indirect mechanisms by characterizing hedgehog-responding mesenchymal cells and testing their contribution using Pdgfrb-Cre-mediated deletion of Smo. The smaller magnitude of dentate effects compared to epithelial Shh deletion (C91) argues against skull dysplasia as the primary mechanism, though the dramatic skull phenotype suggests Ihh involvement (Figure 5).

result: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) of the perinatal dentate gyrus is leaky. At E17.5 and P1, dentate blood vessels were leaky with 70 KDa dye shedding into adjacent cells. Hedgehog-responding dentate cells had endfeet wrapping blood vessels forming neurovascular units. At P5, dentate blood vessels showed significantly weaker integrity compared to CA1 pyramidal zone. Fibrinogen staining and CD41+ platelets were detected in the dentate at E17.5-P1.
evaluation: Claims C7, C35, C79-C85 provide multiple lines of evidence for BBB immaturity in the perinatal dentate using dye perfusion experiments (70 KDa dextran, cadaverine), quantitative comparison to CA1, and markers of vascular permeability (fibrinogen, platelets). The data establish that dentate stem cells could be exposed to blood-borne factors during the critical developmental window (Figure 6).

result: Platelets contain epithelial Shh and provide it to the perinatal DG. Gli1-CreERt2;Rosa-Yfp lineage tracing showed GFP+;DAPI- cells near calvarial sutures and dentate blood vessels were CD42d+ platelets but negative for hematopoietic markers CD34/CD45. Platelets from E17.5 (but not E15.5) blood showed strong Shh expression by immunostaining and Western blot. Krt14-Cre;Shh mutant platelets lost Shh, indicating uptake from dermal sources. Shh gene expression was not detected in platelets. Microvesicles from epidermal cell cultures contained unprocessed Shh proteins.
evaluation: Claims C9-C10, C58-C70 provide extensive evidence that platelets carry Shh from epithelial sources using lineage tracing, multiple antibodies, immunoprecipitation, and genetic loss-of-function. The temporal correlation (E17.5 vs E15.5), loss of platelet Shh in Krt14-Cre mutants (C66-C67), and detection of unprocessed Shh in microvesicles (C69-C70) support a packaging mechanism. Multiple antibody validations strengthen confidence (Figure 7 and supplements).

result: Inhibition of platelet generation using Nfe2−/− mutants reduced hedgehog-responsive dentate stem cells. Nfe2−/− mutants showed reduced platelets in the dentate and dermis at P1, with Shh+;CD41+ platelets reduced to ~30% of normal. Ki67+ dentate progenitors were unchanged at E16.5 but significantly reduced at P1 and P3. Ptch1-LacZ+ cells and Gli1-GFP+ cells were reduced to ~50% at P3 and P1, respectively. Effects persisted through P5.
evaluation: Claims C11, C71-C78 provide functional evidence linking platelets to dentate stem cell development using Nfe2 knockout mice. The temporal specificity (no effect at E16.5, effects from P1 onward) correlates with platelet Shh expression timing. Reductions in multiple hedgehog-responsive markers (Ptch1-LacZ, Gli1-GFP, Ki67, Lef1) provide convergent evidence. The ~50% reduction is consistent with platelets being one of multiple Shh sources (Figure 8).

result: Background on dentate neural stem cells and Shh signaling. Dentate neural stem cells produce neurons throughout life in mammals, and Shh is critical for their maintenance. The perinatal source of Shh is enigmatic. Stem cell niches are established by Shh-responsive radial glial cells appearing at E17. In adults, Shh maintains the niche and drives neurogenesis. Starting at the end of the first week of life, Shh is provided by hilar cells, but Shh-expressing cells are not present when dentate stem cells first appear.
evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C12-C19 establish the scientific context and knowledge gap addressed by the study. These claims are well-supported by multiple citations to prior literature and represent established knowledge in the field. The identification of the knowledge gap (C3, C16) provides clear motivation for the current work.

result: Background on hair follicles, hematopoietic stem cells, and developmental context. Hair follicles produce factors including Shh and establish stem cell niches perinatally through epithelial-mesenchymal interactions. HF development exposes morphogens to nearby stem cell niches. The skull is an active hematopoiesis site during late embryonic development. Megakaryocytes produce various factors, and platelet-deficient mutants have abnormal bone mass. The BBB matures at E15.5 in most forebrain areas except the DG where it matures postnatally.
evaluation: Claims C20-C34 provide essential background on HF biology, HSC development, megakaryocyte/platelet function, and BBB maturation. These claims are well-supported by citations to prior literature and establish the biological plausibility of the proposed mechanism linking HFs, platelets, and dentate development.

result: Discussion context on neurogenesis, platelets, and clinical implications. Disrupted neurogenesis is linked to neurological and psychiatric diseases. Deletion of dorsal Shh using Emx1-Cre or NeuroD6-Cre had modest cortical effects but more significant postnatal DG effects. Platelets regulate hemostasis, wound healing, and tissue repair, and are sources of various growth factors. Platelet-related mutants show vascular and developmental defects. Adult dentate stem cells proliferate in perivascular microenvironments. Youthful circulation rejuvenates aged stem cells in parabionts.
evaluation: Claims C92-C101 provide discussion context relating the findings to broader biological and clinical significance. These claims are supported by appropriate citations and help frame the implications of the work, though they represent prior knowledge rather than new findings from this study.
